jobs.title: Director of Operations (California)
jobs.description:
Western Veterinary Partners is seeking a Director of Operations (DO) to lead a portfolio of veterinary hospitals. The ideal candidate for this role is someone who has successfully managed multiple locations (ideally 10+) in a healthcare, veterinary or multi-site setting. Our ideal candidate is a strong general manager with a goal-oriented attitude, a passion for training and team development, and the business, financial, and strategic acumen to help scale a rapidly growing business and team.

Market Area to include the following geographies:
Northern California and Southern Oregon, including Sacramento, San Jose, Reno, Lake Tahoe, Truckee, Chico, Redding, Medford, Eugene, Salem, and Klamath Falls.

Preferred Home Base:
Sacramento (strongly preferred) or San Jose, or Central Oregon.

In partnership with the Vice President of Operations and Senior Director of Operations, the chosen candidate will focus on supporting veterinary practices in achieving operational excellence, building culture, recruiting and retaining veterinarians, technicians, and support staff. The Director of Operations will spend extensive time in the field with hospital leadership and staff and be responsible for supporting the overall operations of 8 - 12 general practice veterinary hospitals.

About Us

Western Veterinary Partners (WVP) is a mission-driven company based in Denver, CO. We are driven by our values of integrity, alignment, support, collaboration, growth and relationships. WVP is a private equity backed company that acquires, invests in, and supports animal hospitals throughout the United States. WVP is a highly acquisitive company focused on continued growth and expansion into new markets and states. Post-acquisition, WVP supports its partner practices with the non-clinical side of the business. Our local and collaborative support provides veterinarians with attractive operational benefits of a larger group while maintaining the clinical autonomy and local practice identity.

Job Responsibilities

Leadership and Culture

Develop strong relationship with DVMs to assist with recruiting, training, and retention to drive overall business growth
Achieve results through influence and partnership versus through authority or directives
Maintain regular communication with doctors and office staff to review practice trends and performance objectives
Champion WVP’s culture and develop teams and leaders through coaching, mentorship, and programs that deliver on the strategic mission
Provide oversight and support to practice level managers and administrative staff, as well as regional managers
Instill a sense of accountability and service excellence with our teams at all levels
Identify opportunities to improve and maintain site-level employee engagement
Facilitate connections and community among individuals and hospitals within markets and the region
Develop collaborative and productive relationships across the organization
Contribute to growth and innovation across WVP by supporting other geographies and organization-wide initiatives

Financial and Business Objectives

Understand business drivers and create opportunities to optimize them, with a strong focus on volume growth, service mix and offerings, pricing, and margin improvement
Set, manage and exceed WVP’s financial objectives in partnership with sites, regional leaders, and the executive team, with an eye toward future growth opportunities for the company
Provide overall P&L management for the business, along with a vision for near and long-term value creation
Partner with hospital leaders, field operators and functional support to diagnose issues, identify opportunities, and develop corresponding action plans
Employ structured and repeatable management processes with hospital leadership teams to drive operational effectiveness and growth
Prioritize areas of focus based on impact and urgency; help team do the same

Growth and Strategy

Assist in the timely and accurate onboarding and integration of recently affiliated veterinary practices while minimizing disruption to the existing business
Partner with WVP departments (marketing, recruiting, HR, business development, and finance and accounting) to create and implement plans that support business growth, including scheduling optimization, client growth and retention, identification of new services, recruitment of new DVMs, and expansion of existing sites and their capacity
Partner with hospitals to manage DVM capacity, identify and schedule relief, and plan for succession
Nurture and elevate innovation and growth ideas to build tangible, scalable programs
Develop capital budgets for new site development, expansions, and capital equipment purchases, and build and monitor ROI analyses to support business decisions and growth
Forecast future business needs and develop comprehensive strategic plans at the hospital, market, and region levels

Required Criteria

Must reside in Northern CA or Oregon and be open to travel across the state – 70% of the time
5+ years of multi-site operational and/or management experience in fast-growth healthcare services businesses, including previous experience managing a business of similar size and complexity. Previous veterinary experience a plus
Ability to analyze and assess complex and ambiguous data to make recommendations for strategic and operational improvements, leveraging tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, and Tableau
P&L responsibility and experience with budget management, personnel management, and team building
Strong active listening and written and verbal communication skills; Executive presence
Ability to implement processes in collaboration with the VP of Operations to ensure company objectives are met
Highly organized and detail-oriented work ethic
Ability to work collaboratively with all team members, both at the practice level and at the corporate level
Self-directed and able to work independently
Bachelor’s degree required, master’s degree (MBA) highly preferred
Willingness to spend time in the field visiting and supporting affiliated veterinary practices (approximately 70% of time). Occasional travel to Denver and other company activities

The application window will be open for the next two weeks ending 7/31/2026. This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the two--week window.

This role is not open to receiving agency candidates and any contingent submissions will not be honored.

This is a good-faith estimate based on the role's requirements at the time of posting. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. This position is also eligible for bonus and incentive compensation, the terms of which will be provided at the time of offer. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package that may include medical, dental, and vision benefits, vacation, sick leave, 401(k), and other benefits depending on role and location. A complete description of benefits available for this position will be provided during the hiring process. Where required under applicable law, Company provides eligible employees with paid sick leave, health emergency leave, and other legally mandated benefits programs, all in accordance with the requirements of applicable state and local law depending on the location of the practice you support.

jobs.title: Executive Director of External Relations and Engagement (0457U), School of Social Welfare #88417
jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

Berkeley Social Welfare is one of the nation's leading social work graduate programs. As part of the world's top ranked public university, the School of Social Welfare is producing new knowledge for the common good and training the next generation of social work thought leaders dedicated to serving society's most vulnerable members. Known for combining rigorous scholarship with outstanding education, the School of Social Welfare offers MSW and PhD programs as well as an undergraduate major. Since 1944, the School has prepared nearly 12,000 social work professionals for leadership positions in the public and nonprofit human service sectors. Berkeley Social Welfare graduates are dedicated to meeting the growing needs of marginalized, underserved and other vulnerable populations.

This position will assist the Dean in developing new strategic initiatives in education and scholarship. It is modeled after those held by academic program managers in federally sponsored research centers, and in some academic departments, but encompasses the additional complexity of being required to develop a significantly broader network of sponsors from agencies and other external organizations, in addition to academic institutions. Another element of this position will be translating the interests of these various partners and stakeholders into outreach, research and learning activities that engage Social Welfare faculty and students. This position supports the development of a range of scholarly and educational initiatives emphasizing leadership, including undergraduate and graduate courses, certificate programs, a range of professional education options including executive education as well as new domains for inter-professional knowledge building.

Position Summary

The Executive Director of External Relations and Engagement is responsible for providing strategic leadership and operational management across the school’s external engagement functions, including communications, fundraising, revenue-generating programs, events and alumni relations, research development, and instructional technology and design. In addition to managing and developing a team of direct reports, the Executive Director will perform short and long range planning, conduct market research, leverage data to identify and propose new initiatives and revenue streams, and, as needed, liaise with relevant campus departments to accomplish goals.

The Executive Director works closely with the Dean/Associate Dean, a faculty committee focused on revenue generation, and other administrative leaders to ensure goals are on track and met, and may propose high-level recommendations for improvements and/or operational changes to enhance the School’s external engagement.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is September 28, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

External Engagement Strategy and Infrastructure

Acts as key thought partner to the Dean and Senate Faculty on the conception, implementation, management, and scaling of innovative initiatives that involve senior management, faculty, and external stakeholders to extend and enhance the School’s reputation and impact.

Administratively directs initiatives with high autonomy upon approval from the Dean and Senate Faculty, ensuring alignment with School and University goals and policies.
Develops business plans, budgets, and KPIs; assesses and reports on initiative effectiveness and recommends structural or procedural changes to optimize results for assigned programs.
Leads the rebuild of the development and external engagement function; assesses current state and executes a phased implementation plan in partnership with UDAR.

Represents School, in coordination with or in lieu of the Dean, Senate Faculty, and other members of the School, to a network of partners, sponsors, government agencies, multilateral organizations, peer programs, foundations, private donors, alumni, and the public to cultivate and steward relationships with the key research and capacity building partners.

Creates and manages a unified platform for existing and potential community partnerships across government, industry, foundations, and non-profit sectors in Airtable.
Identifies and cultivates new opportunities for collaboration with peer institutions, research centers and groups, and public and private sector partners that advance the educational and research priorities of the school.
Develops scopes of work, pitches, and budgets for new programs, working closely with finance offices and funders to secure necessary resources.
Partners with the Dean to prioritize funding opportunities; oversees the creation and review of scopes of work, pitches, and budgets for new programs, working closely with finance offices and funders to secure necessary resources.
Executes strategic plans for financing programmatic activities, including technical grant-writing and coordination with campus development offices.

Organizes the School’s collective voice in response to legislative, judicial, and social welfare issues to inform local, national, and global policymaking and coordinates with national and global efforts to elevate the voice and impact of social welfare.

Oversees the translation of research findings into policy-relevant knowledge, introducing evidence-based recommendations into ongoing policy dialogues. Liaises with policymakers, program implementers, and journalists to communicate key findings and elevate the School’s public profile.
Reviews and approves critical programmatic outputs, including briefing documents, donor reports, requests for proposals (RFPs), calls for abstracts, peer review protocols, surveys, event concept notes, and agendas, etc.

Revenue Generation, Community Building and Engagement and Program Development

Identifies and prepares concept briefs for new non-degree revenue-generating program ideas to faculty and school leadership, including, but not limited to, continuing education and professional certificate programs.

Works with the instructional design and revenue generation analyst to assess market demand, competitor pricing, implementation timelines, and model multi-year revenue and expense projections for proposed and existing programs to assess viability.
Oversees operational execution of revenue-generating programs including registration, enrollment management, and participant communications; escalates issues to Dean as appropriate.
Tracks program performance against targets; prepares regular reporting for school leadership and recommends adjustments to pricing, format, or marketing.
Works with instructional design and revenue generation analyst and faculty to develop marketable content.

People Management and Team Development

Directly supervises approximately 3.5 FTE staff across communications, fundraising, revenue generation, events and alumni relations, research development, and instructional design.
Creates cross-training opportunities and professional development plans to address the School’s needs and provides ongoing coaching to build team capacity.
Builds and sustains a high performing team culture that reflects the school’s values of inclusion, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
If needed and funds allow, recruits, interviews, selects, and onboards new staff in consultation with SW HR.

Other Duties

May participate in school-wide committees, working groups, and professional development activities as assigned.
Other duties as assigned by Dean or Assistant Dean.

Required Qualifications

Knowledge of external relations functions, such as communications & marketing, development & advancement, and/or government & community relations, and knowledge of how the functions intersect to elevate and enhance an organization’s impact.
Demonstrated experience building or rebuilding a development, advancement, or external engagement program from the ground up, including establishing infrastructure, systems, and operating procedures in alignment with goals, in a resource-constrained environment.
Proven ability to directly supervise and build cohesive, high-performing multi-functional teams in a complex, non-profit environment (including performance assessment, goal-setting, mentoring, coaching, etc.).
Ability to write, edit, and review external-facing communications content, such as donor correspondence, briefs, gift proposals, program pitches, and/or marketing.
Ability to attend and contribute to cultivation events and meetings, including occasional nights and weekends; ability to represent the school professionally to external constituencies including but not limited to alumni, donors, government agencies, and community partners.
Creative and analytical ability to identify, pitch, develop, and successfully implement new programs.
Demonstrated interest in and/or knowledge of program development, building and maintaining relationships with employers in a community, and revenue generation.
Strong financial acumen, including skills in budget development, expenditure monitoring, financial models, projections, in accordance with University financial policies and internal controls.
Demonstrated experience in managing multiple concurrent functions and competing priorities in a complex environment. Strong project management and execution skills.
Excellent interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills; demonstrated ability to work effectively with and build consensus among diverse populations, including faculty; demonstrated expertise building collaborations.
Advanced critical thinking, problem identification and resolution skills; ability to synthesize data from multiple sources to develop recommendations and inform decision-making.
High degree of emotional intelligence and political acumen; excellent ability to maintain confidentiality, objectivity, sensitivity, discretion, professionalism, and exercise good judgment and tact.
Occasional nights/weekends/travel and ability to be onsite a few days a week when not traveling for business.
Knowledge of, or experience with, applicable California state, regional, and local programs, policies, and/or environment in the field of social welfare and/or related fields preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of, or ability to quickly learn, UC Berkeley protocols and administrative systems, including CalAnswers, and familiarity with donor/CRM platforms such as Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce, or CADS.

Education / Training

Bachelor's degree in communications, business, or related field, and/or equivalent experience/training. (Required)
Advanced degree (MBA,MPA,MPP, MSSW or equivalent) in a related field and/or equivalent experience/training. (Preferred)

jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

University Development and Alumni Relations (UDAR) increases support for and enhances knowledge of UC Berkeley through communications, public outreach, and fundraising. The department is responsible for centralized fundraising and donor engagement and works to strengthen unit development offices by consulting and partnering with campus fundraisers. University Development and Alumni Relations also handles a range of central activities and services encompassing events, communications, stewardship, prospect development, gift management, database management, and more.

Position Summary

The Executive Director, Campaign Planning designs, develops, delivers, and administers the University’s comprehensive campaign and associated fundraising programs, working in consultation with campaign counsel and the Vice Chancellor of University Development and Alumni Relations and Associate Vice Chancellor Constituent Programs. This strategic position works closely with campus leadership and fundraising leaders and volunteers to support and deliver measurable annual and long-term outcomes. This position collaborates closely with partners on the development of campaign materials, marketing plans, and organizing related programs/events; it cultivates, stewards, and may solicit donor prospects. This position reports to the Associate Vice Chancellor, Constituent Programs, UDAR with a dotted line report to the Vice Chancellor, University Development and Alumni Relations.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is September 7, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before September 28, 2026. The job will be open until filled.

Responsibilities

Campaign planning and direction

Serves as an expert or lead development professional in campaign planning and direction, which has an environment that includes donors capable of making very significant contributions to the campus.
Develop, implement and assess progress of the campaign plan and recommend overall campaign strategies, including but not limited to campaign architecture (themes, overall goal, sub-goals); Timeline and phases; Volunteer organizational structure; Campaign team budget and staffing.
Collaborate with other UDAR units on campaign stewardship plan; Campaign communications plan; Campaign outreach and events plan.
Conduct and/or oversee the assessment of campaign feasibility and goal setting. Track and report on progress to goal at regular intervals throughout the campaign to high-level campus and volunteer leaders as well as UDAR management team.
Develop and track progress against the campaign timeline and recommend appropriate corrective action and/or campaign adjustments as appropriate.
Serve as primary liaison between UDAR and campaign counsel including scheduling consultation visits and phone calls, as well as receipting invoices and processing of payments.

Campus multidisciplinary themes

In collaboration with the Provost, Vice Chancellor for Research and deans, staff and manage the campus multidisciplinary themes during the public phase of the campaign, including development of transformational gift opportunities as well as identification, cultivation and solicitation of principal and major gift prospective donors.
Staff and manage the ongoing needs assessment and priority setting processes during the public phase of the campaign, including units, programs and other campus initiatives.

Marketing plans/strategies

Develops, creates, writes, implements, and/or evaluates individualized marketing plans and/or strategies for cultivation and solicitation of individual major gifts, gift planning, or corporate/foundation prospects (strategies typically require a high degree of innovation).
Attend meetings where strategies for principal gift-level prospects as well as prospects directly managed by the campaign director are discussed and help ensure that these strategies are developed in the context of the overall campaign strategy.

Executive advisor

Serves as an executive advisor for this area of expertise, interacting with prospects, donors, staff and outside professionals to provide information, advice and counsel regarding specialized program(s).
In partnership with AVC, Constituent Relations and AVC, Development, develop an internal communications strategy to keep colleagues within development/advancement and across the university apprised of campaign priorities, progress, and status.
Attend meetings of UDAR fundraising teams, including PGSI, Major Gifts, and SED, on a regular basis to facilitate coordination with prospects and campaign strategies.
Attend and participate as appropriate in key meetings related to the campaign, such as: Board of Trustees and select committee meetings, as appropriate.
Needs assessment and priority setting meetings.
Campaign volunteer leadership meetings, including unit based advisory groups. Meetings with key stakeholders to plan and implement multidisciplinary themes. Act as campaign liaison to other university offices as appropriate.
Convene specialized communities of practice to promote campaign goals and assessment

Prospect and volunteer constituencies

Creates, establishes and evaluates methods for building/maintaining prospect and volunteer constituencies and identifies, recruits, and directs the activities of high-level volunteers.
Working closely with the Vice Chancellor, provide staffing for the campaign chair/co-chairs and National Campaign Steering Committee, including: scheduling meetings; preparing agendas; briefing the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, and campaign co-chairs; ensuring timely follow-up; and communicating committee decisions to relevant parties within development/advancement and across the university.
Develop individual relationships with NCSC co-chairs and members.
Oversee the development of campaign volunteer resources, such as handbooks, newsletters, and ongoing training opportunities to keep volunteers engaged with the campaign and its priorities, as well as high-level volunteer meetings and events, including the annual Volunteer Summit.

Fundraising and advancement programs / Fundraising goals

Analyzes needs and creates strategic and long-range plans for fundraising and other advancement programs and may have the authority to make commitments and precedent-setting decisions regarding program design, development, and procedures.
Working closely with appropriate colleagues in development/advancement services, including the AVC, Constituent Relations, AVC, PGSI, and AVC, Advancement, develop campaign gift tables, campaign counting and gift tagging protocols, campaign reports, and other tools required to track and report campaign progress, both for campus overall and individual units.
Ensures that predetermined fundraising goals are met.

Campaign team leadership

Manage and provide leadership for the campaign team. Establish and assess overall team strategy and goals. Mentor & coach team members.

Required Qualifications

Expert collaboration, relationship building, and trust building skills to work effectively with a broad range of stakeholders and partners.
Strong ability to navigate organizational complexities and decentralized environments and to lead successfully through influence.
Expert knowledge of comprehensive campaigns, particularly in a university setting.
Expert knowledge of various aspects of and functions in fundraising, such as donor and public relations, communications & marketing, planned giving, stewardship, and/or front-line fundraising, etc.
Expert knowledge of diverse stakeholder groups, teams, departments, achievements, and activities of a major and complex organization, including current issues of concern for both a research university campus and throughout higher education generally.
Expert knowledge of, and/or ability to quickly learn, the UC Berkeley campus including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure; and/or demonstrated success in and expertise of (an) organization(s) with similarities to UC Berkeley.
Expert knowledge of all applicable laws, rules, regulations, risks, etc. in the nonprofit & fundraising field.
Expert written, oral, listening and interpersonal communication skills, including advanced political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships at all organizational levels and with outside constituencies, including donors and volunteers.
Expert skill in making persuasive and compelling presentations of campus goals/objectives and in securing gifts.
Expert analytical, critical thinking, problem solving, and conflict resolution skills.
Expert project/program management skills, including skill in setting and meeting program/project goals and objectives within budget and time constraints.
Demonstrated leadership experience, including the ability to build trust, influence others, and drive results.
Strong skills to lead and develop high-performing team(s), including setting strategic direction, establishing clear expectations, coaching staff, fostering collaboration, and managing accountability.

Coquille Valley Hospital, a Critical Access Hospital located in Coquille, Oregon, is seeking an accomplished and visionary Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the organization through its next phase of growth and innovation. Master’s Degree in Healthcare Administration, MBA or Master’s Degree in a related field.

Strong work ethic, high integrity, outstanding interpersonal skills.

The Organization

Coquille Valley Hospital is a $47M net revenue Critical Access Hospital located in Coquille, OR. The 51,000-square-foot facility was built in 2012. Bond-funded and 100% union-built, the three-story community hospital has 16 beds and 9,000-square-feet of covered parking. As a critical access facility, the hospital offers a broad range of health services for the people of Coquille, Myrtle Point, Powers, Bridge and Fairview, and its state-of-the-art hospital benefits many who visit and live in the Coquille River Valley.

Visit the charming City of Coquille and fall in love with the natural beauty that surrounds it. With direct access to the river, it’s no surprise the city’s residents engage in fishing, hiking, biking and camping and hunting. The individual will initially operate as a highly hands-on leader, supported by existing development, interconnection, finance, and M&A resources.

Develop and own the company's utility-scale energy storage development strategy
Determine priority markets based on congestion, capacity needs, ancillary services, utility procurement activity, interconnection dynamics, and evolving market structures
Originate standalone battery storage projects from concept through advanced development
Build a repeatable framework for identifying attractive POIs, substations, utility territories, and commercial opportunities
Lead early-stage commercial strategy rather than relying on land availability as the primary driver of project origination
Develop relationships with utilities, load-serving entities, commercial counterparties, consultants, and other market participants
Evaluate potential revenue structures including tolling arrangements, capacity contracts, utility procurements, and merchant or partially contracted strategies
Work closely with the interconnection team to evaluate queue position, deliverability, upgrade exposure, and project viability
Partner with finance and investment teams to develop project economics and support investment decisions
Evaluate acquisition opportunities involving standalone storage or broader renewable portfolios
Lead diligence on storage development opportunities presented through the company's M&A pipeline
Establish development processes, market-screening criteria, and portfolio priorities as the storage platform scales
Provide leadership with a clear point of view on where storage markets are heading and where the company should deploy capital
Over time, help build and potentially lead a broader storage development organization

Candidate Profile

The strongest candidates will bring:
Direct experience developing utility-scale standalone battery energy storage projects
A demonstrated understanding of how storage development differs from traditional solar or wind development
Deep knowledge of power markets, storage economics, interconnection, and commercial structures
Experience originating projects based on market fundamentals and commercial opportunity, not simply site control
Strong utility, ISO/RTO, developer, consultant, or commercial counterparty relationships
Experience taking BESS projects from market thesis and origination through advanced development
Familiarity with major organized U.S. power markets; experience across multiple ISOs/RTOs is particularly valuable
Ability to independently form and defend a market thesis using both quantitative and qualitative analysis
Experience evaluating storage acquisitions or conducting development diligence is a plus
Strong commercial instincts paired with practical development execution capabilities
Comfort operating in an entrepreneurial environment without a large dedicated team from day one

This position offers the opportunity to build a storage platform rather than inherit one. For the right candidate, the role also provides a path toward broader development leadership as the company's operating portfolio and development organization expand.

jobs.description:
At Nexteer, our strength lies in the diversity of our team, with each member contributing unique backgrounds, experiences, and aspirations. We believe this diversity fuels our innovation, broadens our perspectives, and propels our collective growth.

For over a century, we have been innovators in the automotive industry. If you are ready to lead change and make a meaningful impact, Nexteer welcomes you.

About The Role

Nexteer is seeking an accomplished, strategic supply management executive to lead Global Supply Management for the US Division. This role is accountable for shaping and executing the division’s supply management strategy across direct and indirect purchasing, advanced purchasing, supplier quality and development, launch readiness, cost competitiveness, supply continuity and resilience.

As a member of the division leadership team, the Executive Director will translate business priorities into an integrated supplier and sourcing agenda. The successful candidate will bring strong commercial judgment, a manufacturing and quality mindset, and the ability to lead through complexity while building trusted partnerships with suppliers and cross-functional leaders.

This position is located in Saginaw, Michigan, with travel expected based on business needs.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Strategy

Lead the US Division GSM organization and establish clear priorities, operating rhythms, decision rights, and accountability across purchasing, supplier quality and development, advanced purchasing, launch, and related supply management activities.
Develop and execute the US Division sourcing and supplier strategy in alignment with global GSM direction, divisional objectives, customer requirements, and financial commitments.
Drive material cost productivity, commercial recovery, working capital improvement, and total cost optimization while protecting quality, delivery, innovation, and long-term supplier viability.

Supplier Performance & Risk Management

Provide executive leadership for supplier performance, including quality, delivery, capacity, launch readiness, supply continuity, risk mitigation, and escalation management.
Ensure sourcing decisions and supplier strategies support new business pursuits, product plans, program milestones, manufacturing requirements, and customer commitments.
Build strategic relationships with key suppliers and lead high-impact commercial negotiations, executive reviews, and issue resolution.
Partner closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, Sales, Program Management, Legal, and global GSM teams to align priorities and resolve complex business challenges.
Anticipate and mitigate supply chain risks through disciplined governance, scenario planning, supplier development, and rapid cross-functional action.

Lead continuous improvement and transformation across GSM processes, analytics, systems, organizational design, and ways of working.
Develop a high-performing leadership team through talent assessment, coaching, succession planning, capability building, and clear performance expectations.
Own the US Division GSM operating budget and contribute to business planning, forecasting, and executive-level performance reviews.
Ensure compliance with company policies, internal controls, applicable trade requirements, ethical sourcing expectations, and internal and external audit requirements.
Represent the US Division in global GSM governance and help shape enterprise-wide strategies, standards, and supplier decisions.

Required Experience

15+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic sourcing, purchasing, supplier management, supplier quality, supply chain, or a related discipline within a complex manufacturing environment.
Demonstrated success leading and developing a sizable supply management organization, with measurable results across cost, quality, delivery, launch execution, risk management, and supplier performance.
Executive-level commercial and negotiation experience, including the ability to manage complex supplier relationships and resolve high-stakes issues.
Strong financial and business acumen, with experience translating business strategy into sourcing priorities, operating plans, and performance commitments.

Leadership Capabilities

Proven ability to lead across functions and influence senior stakeholders in a matrixed, global organization.
Experience leading organizational change, building leadership capability, and strengthening succession pipelines.
Exceptional communication skills, executive presence, sound judgment, and the ability to make timely decisions with incomplete or competing information.

Automotive or mobility industry experience is strongly preferred.
Experience working effectively with global teams and suppliers, with strong cultural awareness and appreciation for diverse perspectives, great sense of diversified culture is preferred.

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, Finance, Operations, or a related field.

The ideal candidate for this role is someone who has successfully managed multiple locations (ideally 10+) in a healthcare, veterinary or multi-site setting. Northern California and Southern Oregon, including Sacramento, San Jose, Reno, Lake Tahoe, Truckee, Chico, Redding, Medford, Eugene, Salem, and Klamath Falls.

Sacramento (strongly preferred) or San Jose, or Central Oregon.

The Director of Operations will spend extensive time in the field with hospital leadership and staff and be responsible for supporting the overall operations of 8 - 12 general practice veterinary hospitals.

About Us

Western Veterinary Partners (WVP) is a mission-driven company based in Denver, CO. We are driven by our values of integrity, alignment, support, collaboration, growth and relationships. WVP is a private equity backed company that acquires, invests in, and supports animal hospitals throughout the United States. WVP is a highly acquisitive company focused on continued growth and expansion into new markets and states. Post-acquisition, WVP supports its partner practices with the non-clinical side of the business. Our local and collaborative support provides veterinarians with attractive operational benefits of a larger group while maintaining the clinical autonomy and local practice identity.

Leadership and Culture

Maintain regular communication with doctors and office staff to review practice trends and performance objectives
Champion WVP’s culture and develop teams and leaders through coaching, mentorship, and programs that deliver on the strategic mission

new_jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

Berkeley Social Welfare is one of the nation's leading social work graduate programs. As part of the world's top ranked public university, the School of Social Welfare is producing new knowledge for the common good and training the next generation of social work thought leaders dedicated to serving society's most vulnerable members. Known for combining rigorous scholarship with outstanding education, the School of Social Welfare offers MSW and PhD programs as well as an undergraduate major. Since 1944, the School has prepared nearly 12,000 social work professionals for leadership positions in the public and nonprofit human service sectors. Berkeley Social Welfare graduates are dedicated to meeting the growing needs of marginalized, underserved and other vulnerable populations.

This position will assist the Dean in developing new strategic initiatives in education and scholarship. It is modeled after those held by academic program managers in federally sponsored research centers, and in some academic departments, but encompasses the additional complexity of being required to develop a significantly broader network of sponsors from agencies and other external organizations, in addition to academic institutions. Another element of this position will be translating the interests of these various partners and stakeholders into outreach, research and learning activities that engage Social Welfare faculty and students. This position supports the development of a range of scholarly and educational initiatives emphasizing leadership, including undergraduate and graduate courses, certificate programs, a range of professional education options including executive education as well as new domains for inter-professional knowledge building.

Position Summary

The Executive Director of External Relations and Engagement is responsible for providing strategic leadership and operational management across the school’s external engagement functions, including communications, fundraising, revenue-generating programs, events and alumni relations, research development, and instructional technology and design. In addition to managing and developing a team of direct reports, the Executive Director will perform short and long range planning, conduct market research, leverage data to identify and propose new initiatives and revenue streams, and, as needed, liaise with relevant campus departments to accomplish goals.

The Executive Director works closely with the Dean/Associate Dean, a faculty committee focused on revenue generation, and other administrative leaders to ensure goals are on track and met, and may propose high-level recommendations for improvements and/or operational changes to enhance the School’s external engagement.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is September 28, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

External Engagement Strategy and Infrastructure

Acts as key thought partner to the Dean and Senate Faculty on the conception, implementation, management, and scaling of innovative initiatives that involve senior management, faculty, and external stakeholders to extend and enhance the School’s reputation and impact.

Administratively directs initiatives with high autonomy upon approval from the Dean and Senate Faculty, ensuring alignment with School and University goals and policies.
Develops business plans, budgets, and KPIs; assesses and reports on initiative effectiveness and recommends structural or procedural changes to optimize results for assigned programs.
Leads the rebuild of the development and external engagement function; assesses current state and executes a phased implementation plan in partnership with UDAR.

Represents School, in coordination with or in lieu of the Dean, Senate Faculty, and other members of the School, to a network of partners, sponsors, government agencies, multilateral organizations, peer programs, foundations, private donors, alumni, and the public to cultivate and steward relationships with the key research and capacity building partners.

Creates and manages a unified platform for existing and potential community partnerships across government, industry, foundations, and non-profit sectors in Airtable.
Identifies and cultivates new opportunities for collaboration with peer institutions, research centers and groups, and public and private sector partners that advance the educational and research priorities of the school.
Develops scopes of work, pitches, and budgets for new programs, working closely with finance offices and funders to secure necessary resources.
Partners with the Dean to prioritize funding opportunities; oversees the creation and review of scopes of work, pitches, and budgets for new programs, working closely with finance offices and funders to secure necessary resources.
Executes strategic plans for financing programmatic activities, including technical grant-writing and coordination with campus development offices.

Organizes the School’s collective voice in response to legislative, judicial, and social welfare issues to inform local, national, and global policymaking and coordinates with national and global efforts to elevate the voice and impact of social welfare.

Oversees the translation of research findings into policy-relevant knowledge, introducing evidence-based recommendations into ongoing policy dialogues. Liaises with policymakers, program implementers, and journalists to communicate key findings and elevate the School’s public profile.
Reviews and approves critical programmatic outputs, including briefing documents, donor reports, requests for proposals (RFPs), calls for abstracts, peer review protocols, surveys, event concept notes, and agendas, etc.

Revenue Generation, Community Building and Engagement and Program Development

Identifies and prepares concept briefs for new non-degree revenue-generating program ideas to faculty and school leadership, including, but not limited to, continuing education and professional certificate programs.

Works with the instructional design and revenue generation analyst to assess market demand, competitor pricing, implementation timelines, and model multi-year revenue and expense projections for proposed and existing programs to assess viability.
Oversees operational execution of revenue-generating programs including registration, enrollment management, and participant communications; escalates issues to Dean as appropriate.
Tracks program performance against targets; prepares regular reporting for school leadership and recommends adjustments to pricing, format, or marketing.
Works with instructional design and revenue generation analyst and faculty to develop marketable content.

People Management and Team Development

Directly supervises approximately 3.5 FTE staff across communications, fundraising, revenue generation, events and alumni relations, research development, and instructional design.
Creates cross-training opportunities and professional development plans to address the School’s needs and provides ongoing coaching to build team capacity.
Builds and sustains a high performing team culture that reflects the school’s values of inclusion, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
If needed and funds allow, recruits, interviews, selects, and onboards new staff in consultation with SW HR.

Other Duties

May participate in school-wide committees, working groups, and professional development activities as assigned.
Other duties as assigned by Dean or Assistant Dean.

Required Qualifications

Knowledge of external relations functions, such as communications & marketing, development & advancement, and/or government & community relations, and knowledge of how the functions intersect to elevate and enhance an organization’s impact.
Demonstrated experience building or rebuilding a development, advancement, or external engagement program from the ground up, including establishing infrastructure, systems, and operating procedures in alignment with goals, in a resource-constrained environment.
Proven ability to directly supervise and build cohesive, high-performing multi-functional teams in a complex, non-profit environment (including performance assessment, goal-setting, mentoring, coaching, etc.).
Ability to write, edit, and review external-facing communications content, such as donor correspondence, briefs, gift proposals, program pitches, and/or marketing.
Ability to attend and contribute to cultivation events and meetings, including occasional nights and weekends; ability to represent the school professionally to external constituencies including but not limited to alumni, donors, government agencies, and community partners.

Founded in 1980, Urban Resource Institute (URI) is the nation’s largest provider of domestic violence shelter and support services and a leading provider of housing and services for families experiencing homelessness. The successful candidate will understand that standalone BESS development requires a fundamentally different approach to market selection, commercial strategy, utility engagement, interconnection, site origination, and revenue underwriting.

The individual will initially operate as a highly hands-on leader, supported by existing development, interconnection, finance, and M&A resources.

Develop and own the company's utility-scale energy storage development strategy

Originate standalone battery storage projects from concept through advanced development
Build a repeatable framework for identifying attractive POIs, substations, utility territories, and commercial opportunities
Lead early-stage commercial strategy rather than relying on land availability as the primary driver of project origination
Develop relationships with utilities, load-serving entities, commercial counterparties, consultants, and other market participants
Evaluate potential revenue structures including tolling arrangements, capacity contracts, utility procurements, and merchant or partially contracted strategies
Work closely with the interconnection team to evaluate queue position, deliverability, upgrade exposure, and project viability
Partner with finance and investment teams to develop project economics and support investment decisions
Evaluate acquisition opportunities involving standalone storage or broader renewable portfolios

Direct experience developing utility-scale standalone battery energy storage projects
A demonstrated understanding of how storage development differs from traditional solar or wind development

Experience originating projects based on market fundamentals and commercial opportunity, not simply site control

Experience evaluating storage acquisitions or conducting development diligence is a plus
Strong commercial instincts paired with practical development execution capabilities
Comfort operating in an entrepreneurial environment without a large dedicated team from day one
